resources.string: VzSync sends a folder from your phone to a GitHub repository in just a few taps. It handles the Git commands for you, no need to open Termux.
In 4 steps
1. Connect your GitHub account with a personal token.
2. Choose your project folder or clone an existing repository.
3. Tap \"Push to GitHub\".
4. Choose to create a new repository or push to an existing one.
If the folder doesn\'t have a Git repository, VzSync creates one automatically. You don\'t need to do anything manually.
What happens under the hood appears in the log, in terminal format. If you already know Git, you can follow each command. If not, the log serves as a record of what was done.
GitHub doesn\'t let apps access your account with a password. Instead, you create a Personal Access Token (PAT) with specific permissions.
Why it\'s needed
Every operation (listing repositories, creating a new one, sending files, cloning) must be authenticated. The token is the credential that proves to GitHub it\'s you acting.
Required scopes
repo — Read and write to repositories.
workflow — Trigger GitHub Actions workflows.
read:user — Read your profile data.
delete_repo — Delete repositories (optional).
How to create it
On GitHub: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token. Check the scopes above and copy the token. You\'ll only see the token once.
Never share your token. It gives full access to your repositories. If it leaks, revoke it immediately on the same screen where you created it.
VzSync stores the token encrypted on your device. It never leaves the phone, except to GitHub itself.
Modern Android doesn\'t let apps access files freely. When you choose a folder, the system gives VzSync a specific permission only for that folder.
Why the path shows as /storage/emulated/0/…
That\'s the real path of the internal storage on Android. In the log, VzSync shows only the end of the path (for example, /…/VzSync) to save space.
The permission is remembered
Once chosen, the folder is remembered. When you open the app again, it will already have it selected. If the permission is revoked by the system, the app asks you to choose again.
If the folder doesn\'t appear in the picker, check if it\'s not on a cloud provider (Drive, Dropbox). VzSync needs direct access to the file system.
The side menu shows the file tree of the selected folder. Open it by tapping the hamburger icon in the bar with the folder name.
How to navigate
Tap a folder to expand or collapse.
Folders with a single child are expanded automatically.
Folders with 2 or more items must be expanded manually.
If the structure is wider than the screen, drag to the side to see the rest.
Ignored folders and files
By default, the menu hides heavy or irrelevant folders: .git, build, node_modules, .gradle, .idea, __pycache__, .cache, target, dist and out.
The tree is only for viewing. VzSync doesn\'t open or edit files — for that, use an external editor.
Pushing in VzSync follows exactly the same flow you\'d do in the terminal. The difference is that the commands are executed by the app.
What happens when pushing
git init — creates the local repository, if it doesn\'t exist yet.
git remote add origin — points to the GitHub repository.
git add . — marks all files for sending.
git commit — records the changes with a message.
git push — sends to GitHub.
You can follow each step in the log in real time. Each command appears with the $ symbol in green; each result, in white.
Customization
In Settings → Push system, you choose the default mode, what the app does after the commit (commit only or commit + push), the message template and the log style.
The \"Create repository\" option creates a new repository on GitHub and sends the entire project at once.
Repository name
GitHub doesn\'t allow spaces or uppercase letters in repository names. VzSync adjusts the name automatically:
Trying Sistema → tentando-sistema
Visibility
Public — anyone can see the repository. Unlimited Actions minutes.
Private — only you can see it. 2,000 min/month Actions limit (free plan).
If you use GitHub Actions to build the project, private repositories consume minutes. Public repositories have unlimited minutes.
The \"Existing repository\" option sends the project to a repository already on your account. You choose between two push modes.
Sync (default)
Keeps the files already in the repository. Only sends what changed. It\'s a normal, safe, reversible push.
Rebuild
Deletes all the current repository content and recreates it from the folder. Useful when you\'ve reorganized the project and want GitHub to reflect exactly the local folder.
Rebuild permanently deletes the remote content. Use only when you\'re sure. The Git history is preserved, but the current files disappear before being recreated.
When in doubt, choose Sync. It\'s always safer, and you can rebuild later if needed.
Cloning means downloading an existing repository from GitHub to your phone. Once cloned, you can edit the files with any editor and send them back through VzSync itself.
How to use
1. Tap \"Clone repository\" on the home screen.
2. Paste the HTTPS URL of the repository.
3. Confirm and wait for the download.
Where the project is saved
Cloned repositories are stored at /storage/emulated/0/VzSync/Repos/{name}. If a folder with that name already exists, the app adds a suffix (name-2, name-3) to avoid overwriting.
Accepted URL formats
https://github.com/user/repo\nhttps://github.com/user/repo.git\nhttps://github.com/user/repo/
SSH URLs (git@github.com:user/repo) don\'t work. Always use HTTPS.
Private repositories work if your token has the \'repo\' scope. Download progress appears in a persistent notification — you can minimize the app or even lock it and the clone keeps running.
Cancel and hide
During the clone, you can hide the screen to keep using the app (the download continues in the background), or cancel to abort. The cancel option also appears in the notification.
The .git folder is where Git stores the entire project history: every commit, every change, and the information of where to push (remote).
If the folder doesn\'t have .git
VzSync creates it automatically. It runs the equivalent of:

git init
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
git add .
git commit -m "…"
git push -u origin main
This is exactly what you\'d do in the terminal. The app does it for you to eliminate friction.
Don\'t delete the .git folder manually. If you do, the app will recreate it and the previous commit history will be lost on the next push.
For projects you already version on PC, copy the entire folder including .git. This way VzSync uses the same remote already configured.
In Settings → Push system, you define how each push behaves. These options apply to all future pushes.
Default push mode
Defines which mode the app already marks as selected on the confirmation screen. You can still change it case by case.
Sync — the safe default. Only sends differences.
Rebuild — deletes and recreates the remote content.
After push
Commit only — saves locally, without sending to GitHub.
Commit + push — the default. Sends to GitHub.
Commit message
It\'s the text that describes each push in the Git history. You can customize it using placeholders. Tap the + button inside the field to see all of them and add to the text.
{date} — current date in dd/MM/yyyy format.
{time} — current time in HH:mm format.
{folder} — path of the folder being pushed.
{repo} — name of the destination repository.
{user} — your GitHub username.
{branch} — target branch (main).
{files} — number of files in the commit.
{mode} — push mode (Sync or Rebuild).
Log style
Both styles show exactly the same information — each command executed and each result. The only difference is visual.
Terminal — real terminal look: commands start with $ in green, results appear in white and errors in red.
Log — each line has a number and a short marker ($, w or e) before the text.
You can switch the style whenever you want. Nothing is lost — only how the log appears on screen changes.
The log shows, in real time, what VzSync is doing. The format depends on the style chosen in Settings → Push system.
Terminal style
$ in green — a command being executed (e.g., git init).
Text in white — success result of a command.
Text in red — error message.
# in gray — explanatory comment from the app.
Log style
$: command — command executed.
w: message — operation completed successfully.
e: message — operation failed.
In both styles, each line has a number on the left and can be selected with a long press to copy.
In Settings → Theme, you choose the app appearance.
AMOLED — fully black background. Saves battery on OLED screens.
Dark — bluish dark background, more comfortable for night reading.
Light — white background, ideal for well-lit environments.
Follow system — uses Android\'s preference.
Changes are applied in real time. No need to restart the app.
The Advanced actions screen gathers manual commands that most users don\'t need day-to-day. VzSync already does the push automatically; these actions are for when you need to intervene manually.
History per repository

Since you can send different folders to different repositories, the history is separated by repository. If you\'ve already pushed to more than one repository, a selector appears at the top of the screen to choose which repository to view.
VzSync tries to automatically select the repository you use with the current folder on Home. If it doesn\'t find one, it uses the most recently used repository.
What is a commit

A commit is a save point of the project in Git. Each commit records what changed, when, why (the message) and who did it. It\'s like a game\'s \"Save\": each commit is a save, and you can return to any of them. VzSync creates a commit with every push.
Commit history
Lists all commits made by VzSync in the selected repository. Each card shows message, branch, hash, source folder and exact date/time. It\'s read-only — nothing is changed.
View last commit
Shows the complete details of the most recent commit in a panel. Includes hash, repository, branch, date, mode (initial, sync or rebuild) and source folder.
Undo last commit
Removes the last commit of the selected repository from local history, but keeps the files. It\'s like undoing the \"save\" without losing progress.
Undo only removes from local history. If the commit was already pushed to GitHub, it stays there. To remove it from GitHub, another process is needed (force push), which VzSync doesn\'t do.
Discard local changes
Discards all changes that haven\'t been committed in the current folder. Files return to the last commit state. No going back.
This action deletes changes you made and didn\'t commit. Use only when you\'re sure nothing there needs to be saved.
Switch branch
Changes the active branch of the repository. If you work with multiple branches (main, dev, feature-x), this lets you tell VzSync which to use on the next push.
The discard changes and switch branch actions only work fully when the real JGit is integrated. For now, they save the intention and show a warning.
The \"My repositories\" screen lists all repositories in your account — public and private — with statistics and quick access to each one.
What you see in the list
Repository name, with a padlock icon if private.
Description, main language, number of stars.
Last updated date.
Filters
At the top of the list, the chips \"All\", \"Public\" and \"Private\" filter the view. The number in parentheses shows how many repositories exist in each group.
Repository details
Tap any repository to open a panel with full details: visibility, default branch, language, stars, forks, watchers, open issues, size in MB, file count and last updated date.
The file count uses the Git tree API. On very large repositories (thousands of files), it may fail and show as \"—\".
Open on GitHub
The \"Open on GitHub\" button in the details panel opens the repository directly in your phone\'s browser.
Delete repository

In the same details panel, the \"Delete repository\" button starts permanent deletion. A confirmation dialog appears explaining that everything will be erased (code, commits, issues, releases, settings).
Deleting a repository is permanent. There\'s no \"undo\". If you need the content, fork or clone before deleting.

For the deletion to work, your GitHub access token needs the \'delete_repo\' scope. If you didn\'t check this scope when creating the token, the operation will fail with error 403. In that case, generate a new token with the extra scope and reconnect in Settings → Account.
VzSync is built on open tools. This section explains how it works under the hood, for those with technical curiosity.
JGit

All Git operations (init, add, commit, push, clone) are done with JGit, a complete implementation of Git in Java maintained by the Eclipse project. It runs locally on your phone — no intermediary server. Your files and your token never pass through us.
Why not use the system\'s native Git

Android doesn\'t come with Git installed by default. Bundling a native Git binary would require cross-compilation for each architecture (arm64, x86_64) and add dozens of megabytes to the APK. JGit runs directly on Android\'s JVM, without external dependencies.
Jetpack Compose
The entire app interface is built with Compose, Google\'s modern toolkit for declarative UIs. This lets the interface react to state changes instantly.
GitHub API

Operations that depend on GitHub (listing repositories, creating a repository, fetching profile) use the official REST API. The token is stored encrypted on the device and never leaves the phone, except in direct calls to GitHub itself.
Project philosophy
VzSync was born to eliminate the friction of pushing code from a phone. It\'s not an editor, not an IDE, not a file manager. It\'s a push button, and it does that well.
The complete list of libraries used, with their licenses, is in Settings → Libraries.
The token doesn\'t work
Check if the token has the required scopes (repo, workflow, read:user) and if it hasn\'t expired. If you revoked the token on GitHub, you need to generate a new one.
No repository appears to choose
Make sure your account has at least one repository. If you just created one, it may take a few seconds for the GitHub API to reflect. Try the refresh button.
The folder isn\'t detected
Folders on cloud providers (Drive, Dropbox) don\'t work. Choose a folder from internal storage or an SD card.
The push failed
Read the message in the log. The most common causes are: expired token, no internet connection, or the remote repository has changes you don\'t have locally. Reopen the app and try again.
The clone failed
Check if the URL is correct (only GitHub HTTPS) and if your connection is stable. If it\'s a private repository, the token needs the \'repo\' scope.
I can\'t delete a repository (error 403)
Your token doesn\'t have the \'delete_repo\' scope. Generate a new token on GitHub checking this extra scope and reconnect in Settings → Account.
The clone notification doesn\'t appear
Check if you allowed notifications for VzSync. On Xiaomi, the system can block notifications from background apps — open System Settings → Battery and allow \"No restrictions\".
Can I use multiple projects?
Yes. Just change the folder on Home (three dots at the top → Change folder) or clone a new repository. Each push uses the current folder.
What happens if I uninstall the app?
Your folders and repositories remain intact. What is lost are local settings (token, selected folder). You reconnect on the next installation.
Push
Sending commits from your computer (or phone) to a remote repository like GitHub.
Commit
A record of changes in Git. Each commit has a message that describes what changed.
Branch
A parallel line of development. The default branch is usually called main or master.
Remote
The address of the remote repository (usually on GitHub). It\'s where the push sends the changes.
Clone
Downloading an entire remote repository to your device, including all commit history.
Fork
An independent copy of a repository. It\'s a way to keep the content before deleting the original.
git init
Command that creates the .git folder in a directory, turning it into a Git repository.
PAT
Personal Access Token. It\'s the credential the app uses to access GitHub on your behalf.
SAF
Storage Access Framework. It\'s the Android system that allows apps to access files with the user\'s permission.
Actions
GitHub Actions. GitHub service that runs automated tasks (like building the project) when you push.
